incongruous

in-KONG-groo-us -- from Latin in- ('not') + congruere ('to agree, come together'), the same root as congruent. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Incongruous is not in harmony or agreement with its surroundings; out of place.

The gleaming glass skyscraper looked strangely incongruous next to the centuries-old stone chapel beside it.

Example

A single bright red balloon tied to the somber funeral wreath struck everyone as deeply incongruous.

The cheerful balloon clashes sharply with the mournful setting -- that mismatch, that sense of not belonging, is exactly what incongruous describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

inconsistent: Inconsistent means failing to stay the same -- an account that changes with each telling, a rule enforced one day and ignored the next. Incongruous is about place, not time: a thing that clashes with its surroundings. Stories are inconsistent; a top hat at a beach party is incongruous.

jarring: Jarring names the effect on you: something so harsh or unexpected that it gives you a small jolt, like a wrong note in a melody. Incongruous names the mismatch itself -- a detail that does not belong in its setting. An incongruous detail is often jarring, but jarring things needn't be out of place.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

harmonious: forming a pleasing and consistent whole

fitting: appropriate to the situation

Where it sits · how badly the parts clash — mismatched → incongruous → discordant

mismatched vs. incongruous: Mismatched is milder than incongruous: mismatched socks merely fail to pair with each other, while an incongruous detail clashes with everything around it and makes the whole scene feel wrong.

discordant vs. incongruous: Discordant is harsher than incongruous: an incongruous detail quietly fails to belong, but discordant elements grate openly against one another, like a trumpet blaring over a string quartet.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin)

prefix — con-

prefix — con-: together, with (Latin)

root — -gru-

root — -gru-: to agree, come together (Latin (congruere))

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of, having the quality of (Latin (-osus))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin congruere meant 'to agree, come together'; with in- ('not') in front and -ous ('having the quality of') at the end, incongruous describes what fails to agree with its surroundings.

Use the root in a new word: congruent

Use the root in a new word: congruent: Ms. Alvarez had us cut out pairs of congruent triangles for the tiling project.

Word Choice

Incongruous almost always describes a mismatch that a person notices and finds a little jarring or funny -- a detail, object, or tone that clashes with everything around it.
